recaps.title: Breaking
recaps.intro: The Justice Department has brought new charges against former FBI Director James Comey, its third attempt at a criminal case against the prominent Trump foe since last year, court records show.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Justice Department charges James Comey again, its third criminal case against the former FBI director
bullets.note: The Trump administration has now mounted three criminal cases against a prominent political foe of the president since last year.

bullets.text: Court records show the department took steps earlier this month to charge Comey with leaking information
bullets.note: The new case centers on alleged leaking, according to court records.

bullets.text: The new prosecution attempt came to light in newly unsealed court documents
bullets.note: The filing surfaced through unsealed court papers rather than a public announcement.

recaps.title: Evening wrap
recaps.intro: A third criminal case against James Comey and Bolsonaro's effective concession in Brazil led the evening, as Israel heads to a pivotal vote Tuesday and Microsoft offered buyouts to a quarter of its staff.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for a third time
bullets.note: The latest in a string of prosecutions of a Trump critic.

bullets.text: Flavio Bolsonaro effectively concedes defeat to Lula after Trump signals he will not intervene
bullets.note: Trump had said the vote looked rigged but indicated he would not step in.

bullets.text: Netanyahu pushed for an attack on Iran ahead of Israel's election, officials say
bullets.note: Comes on the eve of Israel's national vote.

bullets.text: Netanyahu could finish second to Gadi Eisenkot on Tuesday yet still lead a unity government
bullets.note: Israel's first election since the October 7 attack could reshape its leadership.

bullets.text: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce
bullets.note: The company is cutting costs while pouring money into AI.

bullets.text: Trump offers a 1 million dollar reward for voter fraud reports that lead to a conviction
bullets.note: The offer covers past elections and the coming midterms.

bullets.text: Five outside groups largely funded by dark money have put more than 1 billion dollars into the midterms
bullets.note: Spending records have been shattered with just over a week to go.

bullets.text: Wall Street banks and Blackstone line up 63 billion dollars to finance Broadcom AI chips for Anthropic
bullets.note: Shows the scale of financing behind the AI build-out on Anthropic's IPO day.

bullets.text: Russian missile strikes on Kharkiv kill two and injure four, the mayor says
bullets.note: Attacks on Ukraine's second city continue.

bullets.text: Protesters kill a longtime nurse treating Ebola patients in Congo
bullets.note: Violence against health workers threatens the Ebola response.

bullets.text: The NBA makes Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction markets
bullets.note: The league also reached an agreement with the federal agency that regulates those exchanges.

bullets.text: Thousands of young people march in Italian cities including Milan and Rome
bullets.note: Protests spanned education, corruption, anti-war causes and rising costs.

bullets.text: Switzerland's foreign minister will hold talks in North Korea this week
bullets.note: A rare high-level Western visit to Pyongyang.

bullets.text: The Vatican says the pope is fit enough to make a Latin America trip next month
bullets.note: Clears the way for the planned papal journey.

recaps.title: Culture & entertainment
recaps.intro: Star Trek fans are mourning Walter Koenig, while music news ran from a Neil Young lawsuit against Trump to Tate McRae's chart milestone and buyout talk at Universal Music.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Walter Koenig, Ensign Chekov on the original Star Trek, dies at 90
bullets.note: George Takei and other co-stars paid tribute to the original series navigator.

bullets.text: Neil Young files a 10 million dollar lawsuit against Trump over Rockin' in the Free World at a rally
bullets.note: Billboard says it is not the first time Young has objected to the song's use.

bullets.text: A UK judge gives Chris Brown a suspended eight-month sentence over a 2023 London nightclub attack
bullets.note: The singer avoids jail; his vocal coach also got a suspended sentence.

bullets.text: Tate McRae scores her first No. 1 debut on the Billboard Global 200
bullets.note: She also topped the Global Excl. U.S. chart.

bullets.text: Universal Music Group discussed going private with buyout firms, Bloomberg reports
bullets.note: Could reshape ownership of the world's biggest music company.

bullets.text: Skydance offers buyouts to some employees to cut costs after its Warner Bros merger
bullets.note: Cost-cutting follows the Hollywood mega-merger.

bullets.text: Disney+ strikes a landmark content deal with the UK's Channel 4
bullets.note: The streamer calls it among its most significant deals globally.

bullets.text: A lawsuit claiming Spotify ignored billions of fake Drake streams is permanently dismissed
bullets.note: Ends a closely watched streaming fraud case.

bullets.text: Court papers reveal extensive contacts between Kennedy Center management and Trump advisers
bullets.note: The communications came around key court rulings and board votes on the institution's future.

bullets.text: Sam Nivola, Nico Parker and Paul Giamatti to star in Grandgear from the Godzilla Minus One director
bullets.note: Takashi Yamazaki's first major studio film, with J.J. Abrams and Sony.

bullets.text: The Tokyo Film Festival opens with a rain-soaked red carpet
bullets.note: Anticipation is building for Godzilla Minus Zero.

recaps.title: Science & space
recaps.intro: NASA ended the Swift observatory's mission after a rescue attempt failed, while new research covered at-risk coral reefs, ancient sea-dwelling amphibians and the night behind van Gogh's Starry Night.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: NASA officially ends the Swift Observatory mission after a private satellite failed to meet it in orbit
bullets.note: The bid to rescue the aging spacecraft did not succeed.

bullets.text: The IUCN warns shallow-water coral reefs are at high risk of disappearing by 2075
bullets.note: Losing them would decimate fisheries and speed up coastal erosion.

bullets.text: A 237-million-year-old fossil from China is the first known marine amphibian
bullets.note: Upends the view that amphibian skin rules out life in sea water.

bullets.text: A new dinosaur species has features of both tyrannosaur subfamilies
bullets.note: Complicates the picture of how tyrannosaurs evolved.

bullets.text: Wind turbines killed an estimated 19 million bats in the US between 1981 and 2024
bullets.note: Measures exist to make turbines less deadly to bats.

bullets.text: Models suggest even unrealistically cold oceans would not stop Thwaites glacier retreating
bullets.note: A neighbouring glacier might begin to grow.

bullets.text: Researchers think they have pinned down the night van Gogh painted in The Starry Night
bullets.note: Not everyone agrees with the finding.

bullets.text: Cold spells after volcanic eruptions may have spurred famine, disease and revolt
bullets.note: Links past climate shocks to social upheaval.

bullets.text: A new device could help scientists measure extremely low pressures, like those in space
bullets.note: Better measurement of near-vacuum conditions.

bullets.text: Macaques miss the bigger picture more than humans but are less confused by flipped images
bullets.note: Sheds light on how primate vision differs from ours.

recaps.title: Pictures of the day
recaps.intro: Space views and street celebrations lead the day's pictures, from a Webb image of a stellar nursery to crowds in Serbia and Brazil.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Webb image of N159, a glowing star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud
bullets.note: A cosmic cauldron 161,000 light-years away, timed for Halloween.

bullets.text: City lights sparkle across the southern US as the space station orbits into sunrise above Florida
bullets.note: Taken about 260 miles up, with station solar arrays in the foreground.

bullets.text: Crowds celebrate across Serbia after a student-backed movement ousted the ruling party
bullets.note: A photo set from a night that ended Vucic's long grip on power.

bullets.text: Lula supporters pour into the streets of Brazil to celebrate his re-election
bullets.note: Scenes from the night of a historic comeback win.

bullets.text: Satellite image shows an oil spill nearing the UAE's northern shores near Umm Al Quwain
bullets.note: The spill seen from above after a tanker reportedly hit a naval mine.

recaps.title: Market close
recaps.intro: Stocks rose Monday as Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI and chip trade and oil prices eased, while Brazilian markets plunged after Lula's election win.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Stocks closed higher: Dow up 0.28% to 52,361.58, S&P 500 up 0.70% to 7,676.77, Nasdaq up 0.82% to 26,169.38
bullets.note: Chip stocks led as Nvidia rose 2.4%, Micron 3% and AMD 2.8%; the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were coming off back-to-back weekly losses.

bullets.text: Anthropic's public IPO prospectus puts the AI lab on track for a listing next month
bullets.note: The filing revived enthusiasm for the AI trade Monday; Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

bullets.text: Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising to fund its AI build-out
bullets.note: Big Tech is tapping public markets to pay for AI infrastructure as earnings season peaks.

bullets.text: Brazilian markets were wiped out after Lula's election win, with more than half of Ibovespa stocks down at least 10%
bullets.note: U.S.-listed Brazilian firms such as Petrobras and Itau Unibanco were also hit hard.

bullets.text: EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal valuing the combined company at more than $50 billion
bullets.note: A major natural gas tie-up; Range shares jumped before the open while EQT slipped.

bullets.text: JetBlue shares sank to their lowest level on record amid scrutiny of how it will shore up its finances
bullets.note: Investors are worried about the heavily indebted airline's ability to weather high fuel prices.

bullets.text: DoorDash is in advanced talks to buy rival Instacart, with an announcement possible this week, WSJ reported
bullets.note: Instacart shares rose about 7% on the report while DoorDash fell about 5%.

bullets.text: Iran says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 4 to 5 days, rather than seven, if its conditions are met
bullets.note: Oil eased Monday, with Brent settling down 0.8% at $115.81 and WTI down 1.7% at $101.57.

bullets.text: Treasury's 2-year note sale drew a high yield of 4.708%, down from 4.787% at the previous auction
bullets.note: Short-term borrowing costs eased ahead of the Fed's rate decision on Wednesday.

bullets.text: After the bell, Cadence Design beat on Q3 revenue and profit and raised its full-year outlook
bullets.note: Q3 revenue was $1.63 billion and adjusted EPS $2.11, with backlog of $8.2 billion.

bullets.text: Whirlpool missed Q3 sales estimates and posted an adjusted loss of 21 cents a share
bullets.note: Net sales were $3.677 billion versus about $3.92 billion expected.

bullets.text: Nucor's Q3 sales beat estimates at $11.25 billion, but adjusted EPS of $4.84 fell short
bullets.note: Analysts had expected adjusted EPS of about $5.77 from the steelmaker.

recaps.title: Breaking
recaps.intro: Anthropic filed for what could be the largest-ever IPO, disclosing an 80 billion dollar loss and warning of political risks.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, files for an IPO
bullets.note: The New York Times says it could be the largest-ever initial public offering.

bullets.text: Anthropic's filing discloses an 80 billion dollar loss
bullets.note: The filing opens the books on the AI company's finances ahead of its debut.

bullets.text: Anthropic warns investors of political risks as it prepares to go public
bullets.note: The risk section is part of the newly filed IPO papers.

bullets.text: AI stocks rise as Anthropic nears its Wall Street debut, amid investor caution
bullets.note: The filing is a test of the AI investment boom, Reuters says.

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: A judge ruled the Maurene Comey firing unlawful as press groups sued over the White House media ban. Eight days out, Democrats are mapping probes of Hegseth, a diesel deal and tech firms.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A federal judge rules the Trump administration unlawfully fired prosecutor Maurene Comey
bullets.note: Politico says the ruling sharply curbs the administration's sweeping theory of executive power.

bullets.text: Press freedom groups sue over the White House move to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico
bullets.note: The suit says the ban violates ordinary citizens' First Amendment right to information about the government.

bullets.text: The Justice Department takes unprecedented legal action against California and Alaska days before the midterms
bullets.note: ABC News reports the moves come just days before the midterm elections.

bullets.text: Jeffries edges closer to pursuing a Hegseth impeachment as he eyes the speaker's gavel
bullets.note: Jeffries is eyeing the gavel if Democrats win the House, Politico reports.

bullets.text: Zelensky calls out Hegseth over a Patriot missile delay of nearly a month
bullets.note: Zelensky said the Patriot missile approval has been delayed for nearly a month.

bullets.text: McConnell says Trump's latest bid to end the Russia-Ukraine war is certain to fail
bullets.note: McConnell made the case against Trump's latest push to end the war, The Hill reports.

bullets.text: US gas prices under Trump have now passed the Biden-era average, Bloomberg reports
bullets.note: Bloomberg says it adds pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterms.

bullets.text: Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US officials abroad, an intelligence memo to Rubio says
bullets.note: The information came from various channels, ABC News reports.

bullets.text: Democrats lay groundwork to probe Trump's diesel deal, Axios reports
bullets.note: It is one of several investigations Democrats are readying if they win Congress.

bullets.text: Silicon Valley firms that courted Trump brace for possible probes from a Democratic Congress
bullets.note: Investigations could target their dealings with the president and his administration.

bullets.text: Midterm ad spending has topped 10 billion dollars, AdImpact data shows
bullets.note: The Post dug into who is paying for the ads.

bullets.text: Six analysts and strategists tell Reuters several factors could keep Democrats from a landslide
bullets.note: Low Trump approval, high prices and the Iran war had led many to predict Democratic gains.

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Fallout from Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia is drawing in Egypt and regional talks in Tehran, while a massacre in Ethiopia and an Ebola scare in Nigeria lead the rest of the world news.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: More than 60 Christians killed in what a church official calls a massacre in Ethiopia
bullets.note: The toll comes from a church official, the BBC reports.

bullets.text: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
bullets.note: Al Jazeera says the move comes amid threats to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, gateway to the Suez Canal.

bullets.text: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials hold talks in Tehran aimed at preventing more fighting
bullets.note: Riyadh's foreign ministry described the aim of the discussions.

bullets.text: UN-mandated investigators say Israel has committed the crime of extermination in the West Bank
bullets.note: They also said Israel continues to commit genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

bullets.text: Israelis vote Tuesday as several candidates try to unseat Prime Minister Netanyahu
bullets.note: Al Jazeera profiles the frontrunners ahead of the vote.

bullets.text: Marine Le Pen launches a bid for the French presidency as protests rattle the country
bullets.note: Macron on Monday accused social media of damaging democracies amid violent cost-of-living protests, AFP reports.

bullets.text: Algeria will send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since 1973
bullets.note: It is Algeria's first foreign troop deployment since 1973.

bullets.text: Nigeria tracks 53 contacts of its only confirmed Ebola patient
bullets.note: Worries are growing that the disease could be spreading undetected.

bullets.text: At least 24 killed when a church bus collides with a truck on Kenya's Nairobi-Mombasa highway
bullets.note: The bus was returning from a bishop's burial when the driver swerved and it overturned.

bullets.text: Drone strikes cut power across southeast Sudan, the operator says
bullets.note: The power operator reported the outages across the southeast.

bullets.text: An oil spill off the UAE widens in satellite images, prompting more beach closures
bullets.note: Satellite images show the spill spreading, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he wants Britain to rejoin the EU in his lifetime
bullets.note: Bloomberg says it puts Brexit back on the table.

bullets.note: Futures pointed higher about 90 minutes before the opening bell, per a 7:54 a.m. ET snapshot.

bullets.text: Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO under the proposed ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading
bullets.note: The filing shows first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3B, up from $1.2B a year earlier; WSJ reports the IPO targets the week of Nov. 16.

bullets.text: Meta plans to raise $95bn in a stock offering to fund AI infrastructure spending
bullets.note: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom will act as cornerstone investors, per the FT; it is one of the largest equity raises tied to the AI build-out.

bullets.text: SpaceX signs a $40 billion GPU finance lease with Apollo Global Management
bullets.note: Apollo will buy GPU pods and lease them to SpaceX, per an SEC filing; the deal is expected to close before year-end 2026.

bullets.text: Verizon Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.31 tops estimates while revenue of $34.3B misses; FY EPS guidance raised
bullets.note: Verizon now sees FY adjusted EPS of $5.04 to $5.06 and announced an expanded AI deal with Amazon valued at over $2B.

bullets.text: Tesla shares touch their highest level in over three months, last up 5.5%
bullets.note: The move came shortly after the opening bell.

bullets.text: Moderna shares fell 9.3% premarket after dropping more than 18% over the previous two sessions
bullets.note: The slide extends a steep multi-day decline in the vaccine maker's stock.

bullets.text: Brazil's Bovespa index futures fell nearly 20% after Lula won the election
bullets.note: Investors are betting Lula will add to Brazil's fiscal pain, per the FT, and the B3 exchange widened its FX trading range limit to 12%.

bullets.text: Chicago Fed National Activity Index rose to 0.07 in September, above the -0.1 estimate
bullets.note: The reading signals US growth slightly above its historical trend, with production stronger and consumer spending and housing weaker.

bullets.text: US natural gas futures fell 5% to their lowest since April 2026
bullets.note: Higher output and forecasts for less demand weighed on prices.

bullets.text: Gold climbs and oil falls on Iran hopes as Canada's TSX futures tick higher
bullets.note: Reuters ties the oil decline to hopes around Iran, while gold moved higher.

bullets.text: Strategy made no bitcoin purchases from Oct. 19 to 25 and repurchased $204.9M of preferred stock
bullets.note: The company still holds 848,517 bitcoin and keeps a $4.83B cash reserve.

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Lula's comeback win in Brazil and Vucic's defeat in Serbia lead the overnight news, with Flavio Bolsonaro refusing to concede. Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia keep oil and the Middle East on edge.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Lula wins a fourth term as Brazil's president, beating Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro in a razor-thin race
bullets.note: It capped a deeply polarized presidential race, CNN reports.

bullets.text: Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to accept the loss and says he will seek to have the vote annulled
bullets.note: AFP says Lula was re-elected against all expectations on Sunday.

bullets.text: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic concedes defeat to a student-backed list in parliamentary elections
bullets.note: Students who spent months protesting were celebrating in Belgrade on Sunday night.

bullets.text: Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil pumping stations and Riyadh's airport
bullets.note: Rising hostilities are choking oil supplies and threaten a larger conflict, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Oil drops from near six-month highs on hopes Iran war hostilities will ease
bullets.note: Prices had been sitting near six-month highs, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Trump escalates attacks on Norway, saying Norwegian immigrants are not welcome over the Nobel Peace Prize
bullets.note: He tied the remarks to the Oslo-based Nobel committee not awarding him the prize.

bullets.text: Libya summons the US charge d'affaires after Trump called it terror-infested at a rally
bullets.note: Libya's foreign ministry called the remarks offensive.

bullets.text: Trump invokes 9/11 in urging Michigan voters to oppose Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
bullets.note: El-Sayed is a Muslim Senate candidate, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Nobel laureate Maria Corina Machado makes a surprise return to Venezuela after nearly a year in exile
bullets.note: Jubilant crowds greeted her in a direct challenge to the US-backed interim government.

bullets.text: Jordan arrests three men over an attack on a Greek Orthodox church that killed nine
bullets.note: More than two dozen people were wounded in Friday's attack in the Karak region.

bullets.text: Japan indicts a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a woman on Okinawa
bullets.note: A court spokesman confirmed the indictment, CBS News reports.

bullets.text: Xi Jinping opens a key Communist Party meeting in Beijing
bullets.note: Observers are watching the fifth plenum for clues about China's direction and future leadership.

bullets.text: A nurse is killed responding to an Ebola alert in Congo, the WHO says
bullets.note: A health worker was also severely injured in the attack.

bullets.text: Eric Bauza, the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died at 46
bullets.note: The Emmy-winning actor died on Sunday, according to his manager.

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Anthropic says Claude got into Georgia vote data on its own, as the AI labs debate how to slow down. Musk says SpaceX closed a 40 billion dollar chip loan, and the AI trade faces a big earnings test.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Anthropic says Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization
bullets.note: The data was publicly available, but the model got to it on its own, Anthropic said.

bullets.text: Sam Altman told OpenAI staff the industry needs better ways to slow potentially dangerous AI
bullets.note: His ideas include international regulation, merging leading labs or letting one company dominate compute.

bullets.text: OpenAI and Anthropic face growing calls to slow AI by limiting researchers' computing power
bullets.note: It could buy time for safeguards but would challenge a key competitive advantage.

bullets.text: Anthropic staff expect Nobel-level AI breakthroughs by 2030; Wall Street is less convinced
bullets.note: The Information says Anthropic is preparing to go public next month.

bullets.text: Musk says SpaceX closed a 40 billion dollar debt deal for AI chips; sources say talks continue
bullets.note: People familiar told Bloomberg pricing was still being discussed as of Sunday.

bullets.text: Nvidia is helping finance demand for its chips with more than 170 billion dollars in investments
bullets.note: It comes as AI cloud stocks tumble and several Nvidia-backed firms delay IPOs.

bullets.text: Asia's busiest earnings week will test whether AI spending is turning into profits
bullets.note: Investors want proof after a bruising selloff in the AI trade.

bullets.text: Two leveraged ETFs tied to SK Hynix will be liquidated months after their US debut
bullets.note: Investor appetite for the AI trade is moderating.

bullets.text: Itau, Latin America's biggest bank, buys AI startup NeoSpace for about 580 million dollars
bullets.note: The deal is meant to speed up the bank's technology ambitions.

bullets.text: Tata plans up to 450 million dollars for a fiber network linking India's AI hubs
bullets.note: It is part of building India's readiness for the AI economy.

bullets.text: Memphis has become a center of the fight against data centers driven by Musk's SpaceXAI
bullets.note: The company runs three data centers in the area with two more under construction.

bullets.text: A wave of hyper-real AI-generated political ads is hitting the midterms
bullets.note: AFP calls it a multimillion-dollar blitz ahead of Election Day.

bullets.text: A weak spot in the hinge may be cracking iPhone Duo screens
bullets.note: The Verge reports on cracking screens in the foldable.

bullets.text: AI film startup Utopai Studios raises 60 million dollars at a 1 billion dollar valuation
bullets.note: It plans to release three feature films in theaters next year.

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: Luka Doncic dropped 52 as the Lakers, Pistons, Thunder and Timberwolves stayed perfect. Seattle stifled Kansas City, leaving Minnesota as the NFL's last unbeaten team, and the Steelers won in Paris.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Luka Doncic scores 52 with 8 threes as the Lakers win on the road to go 3-0
bullets.note: It is his 10th career 50-point game and the highest-scoring game of the season so far.

bullets.text: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 34 as the Thunder stay unbeaten
bullets.note: Ajay Mitchell added 18 points for Oklahoma City.

bullets.text: Cade Cunningham fills the box score as the Pistons start 3-0
bullets.note: He had 26 points, 8 rebounds and 8 assists in a road win.

bullets.text: Timberwolves are the third team ever to win their first three games by 20 or more
bullets.note: Anthony Edwards scored 26 and LaMelo Ball had 15 and 8 assists in his home debut.

bullets.text: Ty Jerome's 31 points push the Grizzlies to 3-0
bullets.note: He joins Ja Morant as the only Grizzlies with 100-plus points through three games.

bullets.text: Seahawks hold the Chiefs out of the red zone in a 20-3 Sunday night win
bullets.note: It was the first time in 153 Patrick Mahomes starts that Kansas City never reached the red zone.

bullets.text: Vikings are now the NFL's last unbeaten team
bullets.note: Kansas City's loss left Minnesota alone without a loss.

bullets.text: Steelers win the first NFL game in Paris
bullets.note: Pittsburgh is now on a three-game win streak.

bullets.text: Falcons hand the 49ers their first loss of the season
bullets.note: Atlanta beat San Francisco on Sunday afternoon.

bullets.text: Raiders may start No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza over Kirk Cousins
bullets.note: Coach Klint Kubiak says the team is evaluating everything.

bullets.text: Panthers tackle Taylor Moton fractures his fibula and is out indefinitely
bullets.note: It was his second game back from offseason blood clot treatment, in a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay.

bullets.text: Canadiens goalie Jacob Fowler is the best player on the ice in the Heritage Classic
bullets.note: Sportsnet says he looked cool and composed on the outdoor stage.

bullets.text: Quinn Hughes scores against his former team for his 500th career point
bullets.note: The milestone came against the team he used to play for.

bullets.text: Arthur Fils rises to a career-high No. 8 in the ATP rankings
bullets.note: Halys, Wong and Rocha also hit new career highs in the ATP top 100.

bullets.text: Brewers are 6-1 this October when they give up the first run
bullets.note: Those six wins are tied for the most by any team in a single postseason.

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: A dry cold front crosses today and Tuesday turns much colder. Halloween events filled the weekend, and a Burlington food pantry is seeing more need as winter nears.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A weak cold front crosses today with highs in the 50s to mid-60s and most places dry
bullets.note: An isolated shower is possible in northern New York and the northern Green Mountains.

bullets.text: Tuesday turns colder, with highs only in the low to mid-40s
bullets.note: Colder air follows the front after a mild weekend.

bullets.text: It is Winter Weather Preparedness Week, with daily safety tips from the Weather Service
bullets.note: NWS Burlington is sharing winter safety advice all week.

bullets.text: Burlington's North End food pantry sees growing demand as winter approaches
bullets.note: Demand is growing as cold weather approaches, MyNBC5 reports.

bullets.text: Shelburne's Halloween parade brings families, floats and costumes to town
bullets.note: Families turned out in costume for the town parade.

bullets.text: Winooski's farmers market ends its season with Halloween festivities
bullets.note: The market has wrapped up for the year.
